newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares fall, period of consolidation ahead.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares fall, period of consolidation ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower in a sour market on Tuesday, with dealers seeing better conditions ahead with a period of consolidation setting in.

"The market is oversold at the moment so I think we will see a period of consolidation in November with the market standing still. There should not be any further falls tomorrow, we expect prices to remain about the same in a market treading water," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.20 point down at 125.93 while the KFX December future fell 1.65 point to 126.45 with 509 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Overall turnover for the day was 614 million crowns.
Among KFX paper, only ISS, GN Store Nord and Carlsberg A bucked the downward trend. ISS closed two crowns higher at 163, GN five up at 615 and Carlsberg two crowns ahead at 371.
A takeover bid for Sweden's Orrefors Kosta Boda glassmaker involving Carlsberg subsidiary Royal Copenhagen came too late, after the bourse closed, to affect the Carlsberg share.
As on Monday, BG Bank was the day's most traded paper, with 163,000 shares changing hands to finish three crowns lower though at 252.
